newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - November 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - November 28.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Thursday.
- Irish Prime Minister John Bruton and British Prime Minister John Major are to hold an Anglo-Irish summit meeting in London on December 9.
- A total of 1,689 people has tested positive for HIV, 549 have AIDS and 293 have died, the latest statistics for the Irish Republic show.

- Representatives of five police divisions have issued statements disassociating themselves from criticism levelled at the Minister for Justice by the general secretary of the Police Representative Association.
- At least 34 licences for the export of military goods have been issued by the Department of Tourism and Trade to two Irish companies this year.
- A price war between Telecom Eireann and its competitors looks set to erupt following the EU's decision on Wednesday to order Ireland to open up the business sector to more competition.
- The government's pay deal hopes suffered on Wednesday as discussions with unions had to be postponed after the government asked for a 12-month pay freeze.
- The lowest referendum turnout in about 20 years is expected to produce a "yes' vote for a change in the bail laws.
- A government minister has returned almost three million Irish pounds earmarked for back-to-work schemes that were not working.
- A training camp for IRA bomb makers has been uncovered by police and troops after a joint search of land off the main Dublin to Belfast road in County Louth.
- Deputy Irish Prime Minister Dick Spring told his labour parliamentary party on Wednesday that the door had not closed on the hopes for an IRA ceasefire.
